chunks: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about the male slave: how many women are permissible for him? He said, 'Two women.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations are specific to the free women (concubines of free status) and not the female slaves. And that which reveals what we mentioned as additional to what preceded is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْحَرَائِرِ: Free women (female slaves of free status)

ai.seo_question: How many wives is a male slave permitted to have according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes that a male slave (*mamluk*) is permitted to marry two women, a ruling derived from the general permissibility of polygyny with specific adjustments for status. The subsequent clarification by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan distinguishes this allowance for free women (*harair*), highlighting the jurisprudential nuance in how marital rights and dowries were calculated differently for slaves versus free persons in Shia fiqh. This reflects the practical application of Quranic principles to the social hierarchy of early Islamic society.
